source.filename: 2022-Soft actuator with switchable stiffness using a micropump-activated jamming system.pdf

control_variables: Electrode pair dimensions: 0.2 mm electrode gap, 0.2 mm slit width, and 0.3 mm slit depth
Electrode pair arrangement: 3 pairs in parallel and 27 pairs in series in each flow direction
Jamming material: aluminium oxide particles with a diameter of 20 µm
Linear stage displacement speed: 0.5 mm/s up to 3 mm total movement distance
Soft actuator base material: SYLGARD 184 silicone elastomer mixed in a 10:1 ratio and cured at 100 °C for 1 hour
Channel and bonding adhesives: EP001N elastic adhesive cured at room temperature for 24 hours
dependent_variables: Bending force at 3 mm displacement (0.134 N to 0.743 N)
Load-bearing capability (ability to hold 130 g tip load)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Embedding a flexible bidirectional electro-conjugate fluid (ECF) micropump directly into a Pneu-Nets soft actuator enables dual-mode operation: active bending via positive hydraulic pressure and stiffness tuning via negative pressure granular jamming.
The fabricated bidirectional flexible ECF micropump generates static pressure up to ±55 kPa and a no-load flow rate up to 140 mm³/s at an applied voltage of 2.5 kV.

Applying negative pressure (-50 kPa at 2.45 kV) to induce granular jamming of 20 µm aluminium oxide particles increases the soft actuator's bending force at 3 mm displacement from 0.134 N to 0.743 N, representing a 5.5-fold stiffness enhancement over the unjammed state.

Under negative pressure activated by 2.5 kV, the stiffened soft actuator can hold an external mass of 130 g at its tip (5.2 times its own weight of 25 g), but drops the load when the voltage is turned off and stiffness returns to the compliant state.
Positive pressure generated by the integrated micropump (+50 kPa at 2.45 kV) produces active bending of the Pneu-Nets actuator up to a 16° bending angle and a 7 mm vertical tip displacement.

The flexible micropump is microfabricated on a polyimide flexible printed circuit board using a modified UV-LIGA process with electroformed nickel microelectrodes, maintaining electrode spacing even under large bending deformations.

experimental_setup: Micropump pressure and flow rate characterization: sealed flexible micropump connected to a pressure sensor to measure static output pressure under no-flow conditions, and an open collection beaker on an analytical scale with timing to determine no-load flow rate across applied voltages from 0 to 2.5 kV in 0.5 kV increments.

Stiffness measurement setup: soft actuator fixed at one base end while a force gauge mounted on a motorized linear stage displaces the free tip by 3 mm at 0.5 mm/s, recording tip reaction force versus displacement at negative pressures from 0 to -50 kPa (voltages from 0 to 2.45 kV).

Load-bearing test: soft actuator clamped horizontally, stiffened with 2.5 kV applied to generate negative pressure, loaded with a 130 g tip weight, and monitored before and after switching off the voltage.

Bending actuation evaluation: actuator mounted horizontally and connected to a high-voltage DC power supply and external ECF fluid reservoir; positive pressure applied from +10 to +50 kPa (1.1 to 2.45 kV); bending angles and vertical tip displacements recorded with a high-resolution camera and vertical scale.
future_work: Improving the bonding technique for the micropump assembly to eliminate asymmetric channel expansion and achieve identical performance in both flow directions.
Fabricating the soft actuator from softer elastomeric materials (such as Ecoflex rubbers) to achieve larger bending angles and displacements.
independent_variables: Applied DC voltage to the ECF micropump (0 to 2.5 kV, specifically evaluated at 1.1 kV, 1.6 kV, 2.0 kV, 2.2 kV, 2.45 kV, and 2.5 kV)
ECF flow direction (positive pressure / forward flow vs. negative pressure / reverse flow)
Tip indentation displacement applied by the linear stage (0 to 3 mm)
limitations_inferred: The system requires kilovolt-level high-voltage DC power supplies (up to 2.5 kV), which introduces electrical insulation concerns and may complicate onboard power electronics miniaturization.
The actuator remains tethered to an external high-voltage supply and an external ECF fluid reservoir tank rather than being fully self-contained or untethered.
Long-term cycling durability, potential particle clogging or wear of the metallic mesh filter, and fluid leakage over extended operation were not investigated.
No theoretical, analytical, or computational constitutive modeling was provided to predict the jamming-induced stiffness or pressure-deflection response.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Due to the compact integrated design, the internal pressure and flow rate inside the assembled actuator could not be measured directly during actuation or stiffness switching; operating pressures had to be inferred from separate no-flow calibration experiments.

A performance discrepancy existed between the two flow directions (11% difference in static pressure and 3% in flow rate), caused by asymmetric expansion of the PDMS channel under positive pressure due to fabrication error.
The maximum bending deformation was relatively modest (16° bending angle and 7 mm vertical displacement) due to the stiffness of the SYLGARD 184 silicone elastomer.
main_results: The bidirectional flexible ECF micropump achieved a maximum output pressure of ±55 kPa and a no-load flow rate of 140 mm³/s at 2.5 kV.
Negative pressure jamming at -50 kPa increased the tip bending force at 3 mm displacement from 0.134 N to 0.743 N, yielding a 5.5-fold increase in actuator stiffness.
The stiffened actuator successfully carried a 130 g tip load (5.2 times its own weight of 25 g), but dropped the load once voltage was removed.
Positive pressure hydraulic inflation at +50 kPa caused Pneu-Nets chamber expansion, producing a maximum bending angle of 16° and a tip vertical displacement of 7 mm.
The flexible micropump on polyimide substrate maintained its structural integrity and electrode gap during significant bending deformation.
performance_metrics: Maximum output pressure: ±55 kPa at 2.5 kV
Maximum flow rate: 140 mm³/s at 2.5 kV
Stiffness increase factor: 5.5-fold (bending force increased from 0.134 N to 0.743 N at 3 mm deflection)
Maximum bending angle: 16° at +50 kPa (2.45 kV)
Maximum vertical tip displacement: 7 mm at +50 kPa
Load-to-weight ratio: 5.2x (130 g payload supported by a 25 g actuator)
Bidirectional asymmetry: 11% difference in static pressure and 3% difference in flow rate between flow directions
possible_gap_implications: Demonstrating that an embedded micro hydraulic source can replace bulky external vacuum pumps and compressors in granular jamming systems helps address the miniaturization bottleneck in variable-stiffness soft robotics. However, achieving practical untethered soft robots will require developing miniaturized high-voltage drivers, onboard closed-loop fluid management, and robust filter interfaces for cyclic durability.
paper.research_objective: To design, microfabricate, and experimentally evaluate a compact soft actuator that integrates an embedded bidirectional flexible electro-conjugate fluid (ECF) micropump to provide both active bending deformation via positive hydraulic pressure and tunable stiffness via negative-pressure granular jamming.
paper.research_problem: Soft robots are compliant and safe for environment interaction, but their inherent flexibility makes it difficult to exert high forces. While granular jamming can provide switchable stiffness, conventional jamming systems rely on bulky external vacuum pumps, compressors, valves, and clunky tubing, hindering miniaturization and practical integration.
paper.title: Soft actuator with switchable stiffness using a micropump-activated jamming system
